content: Baylor College of Dentistry (BCD), situated in east Dallas, Texas, serves as the dental education branch of the Texas A&M University System and is part of the Texas A&M Health Science Center. Approximately two-thirds of all dentists practicing in the Dallas/Fort Worth Metroplex received their education at BCD, and over one-third of all dentists in Texas are alumni of this institution. It is the largest single provider of oral health care services in the Dallas/Fort Worth area. The college was established 100 years ago as the State Dental College, initially admitting 45 students. Today, it has grown to an enrollment of approximately 520 students and boasts over 8,000 graduates. BCD is internationally recognized for its excellence in oral health sciences education, research, specialized patient care, and community service programs. The institution offers degrees such as the Doctor of Dental Surgery (DDS), Master of Science (MS), and Bachelor of Science (BS) in Dental Hygiene, as well as advanced training in dental specialties. Baylor College of Dentistry has been ranked among the top four dental institutions in the United States for periodontology, endodontics, and geriatric dentistry by American Health Magazine. In 1997, the college made history by becoming the first dental school in the nation to successfully utilize telecommunications technology for dental medicine. This was demonstrated through a long-distance patient consultation between dentists at the BCD campus and 175 dental professionals gathered in Orlando, Florida. Each year, the college conducts over 103,500 patient care visits, with 45% of these services benefiting low-income individuals. Additionally, the college donates $3.3 million worth of services to the community annually. BCD also produces the only nationally syndicated weekly dental health news program, Dental Health Check. The academic offerings at BCD include a four-year Doctor of Dental Surgery program, a Bachelor’s degree in Dental Hygiene, multiple Master’s degree programs, and a Ph.D. program in biomedical sciences. Post-doctoral degrees in dental specialties are also available. Furthermore, an M.D. program is offered in collaboration with the Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center in Lubbock. Through its Department of Continuing Education, BCD provides dental professionals from around the world with opportunities to further their education and access cutting-edge dental technologies. In addition to its educational programs, BCD is a nationally recognized center for both basic and clinical research in oral health. The college’s research initiatives extend beyond dental medicine, with faculty exploring advancements in areas such as laser technology, computer-aided dental restorations, improvements in dental materials, craniofacial deformities, and treatments for salivary dysfunction. Faculty members are also conducting research with potential implications for the prevention and treatment of systemic diseases, including Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, cancer, and diabetes. The college is centrally located in Dallas, just one mile east of the downtown business district, and is adjacent to Baylor University Medical Center. Faculty members also oversee dental clinics at two local children’s hospitals and provide oral health care services at the Parkland Health & Hospital System, the Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Dallas, Baylor University Medical Center, and Denton State School.
